title: A REST call and a row, one SELECT apart
description: HTTP Client closes the smallest possible gap between a [REST API](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110) and a DuckDB row: instead of standing up a Python or Node.js sidecar to fetch a payload and load it back in, you call a scalar function inside a `SELECT` and get the response as a [`JSON`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions) value you can extract, cast, and join on the spot. That tight coupling is its whole reason to exist — and also the source of every caveat below. It is built for ad-hoc API calls and low-volume per-row enrichment, not for high-throughput or streaming integrations.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: The extension is a deliberately thin SQL surface over a single synchronous HTTP request — there is no `ATTACH`, no secrets type, no connection pool, no background fetcher, and no retry machinery. Each function call opens a connection, issues the request, blocks until the full response is in memory, and returns it as a JSON struct. Because the function shape is stable and side-effect-free at the SQL layer, the result composes cleanly into CTEs, lateral joins, and `CREATE TABLE AS` — anywhere a scalar JSON value is acceptable.

bulletPoints.label: Synchronous and blocking
bulletPoints.description: DuckDB stalls on each call until the response arrives or the underlying request fails — there is no per-row timeout knob and no async dispatch. A slow endpoint slows the whole query, and rows are processed in whatever order DuckDB chooses to evaluate the scalar.

bulletPoints.label: One call per row
bulletPoints.description: Per-row enrichment issues exactly one HTTP request per input row, sequentially, with no connection reuse exposed at the SQL layer. Fine for tens or hundreds of rows; for tens of thousands it is slow and very likely to get rate-limited upstream. Pre-aggregate to distinct keys or cache responses into a table with [`CREATE TABLE AS`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/create_table) before joining at scale.

bulletPoints.label: JSON response struct
bulletPoints.description: Every call returns a JSON object shaped `{status, reason, body}` — `status` is the numeric HTTP code, `reason` is the [HTTP reason phrase](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#name-status-codes) (`"OK"`, `"Not Found"`), and `body` is always a string. Pull fields out with [`->>`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions); to drill into a JSON response body, cast it first: `((res->>'body')::JSON)->>'$.field'`.

bulletPoints.label: Headers and params are MAPs
bulletPoints.description: Headers and POST parameters are passed as DuckDB [`MAP`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/map) literals — `MAP{'key': 'value', ...}`. Headers go on the wire as-is; how the params map is encoded into the body (JSON vs. URL-encoded form) depends on which POST function you call.

sections.title: Scope and caveats
sections.description: The extension is honest-by-design about what it does not do. Read this before pointing it at production traffic — for anything it lacks (streaming, complex auth, retries, parallelism), keep a real HTTP client or shell out to `curl` via [shellfs](/products/extensions/shellfs).

bulletPoints.label: Experimental status
bulletPoints.description: Marked **experimental** by the [upstream README](https://github.com/Query-farm/duckdb-extension-httpclient) — "USE AT YOUR OWN RISK!". Pin a known-good extension version in any pipeline that depends on it.

bulletPoints.label: GET and POST only
bulletPoints.description: The documented surface covers `GET` and `POST` (JSON or form-encoded) — no `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE`. For other [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods), shell out to `curl` via [shellfs](/products/extensions/shellfs).

bulletPoints.label: No retries, backoff, or streaming
bulletPoints.description: The request is issued once and the entire response body is buffered into memory — there is no automatic retry, no backoff, and no streaming read of large responses. Build retry/backoff in your application layer, and prefer shellfs + `curl` piped through [`read_csv`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/csv/overview) / [`read_json`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/loading_json.html) when a response is too big to hold in memory.

bulletPoints.label: Credentials are visible in the query plan
bulletPoints.description: Any token or secret inlined into a `headers` or `params` map appears in the cached query plan and `EXPLAIN` output. Source credentials from the environment with [`getenv`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/functions/utility#getenv) and bind them through [`SET VARIABLE`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/set) — `getenv` resolves at parse time, so the literal value never lands in a cached plan or session log.
